text:
rachel: quick heads-up — while working on the service token migration I ran into a namespace gap between project-scoped issuance and operator-scoped tokens. seems like a source of confusion for delegation and audit trails. :thinking:
ken: can you sketch the gap? short example helps.
rachel: sure — current model issues tokens either as org-wide operator tokens (long-lived) or project-scoped API keys. we lack a first-class short-lived project delegation token that surfaces provenance for a calling service. leads to two bad patterns: long-lived operator tokens with scoping in code, or opaque project keys that get proxied.
sam: ugh, yeah. that's bite-sized tech debt. what about ephemeral tokens with a "delegation ledger" claim — minted by auth-service with parent_token_id and requestor_service fields?
rachel: exactly. prototype claim payload I used: 
```
{
  "iss": "auth.redwood",
  "sub": "svc:ingest",
  "aud": "project:alpha",
  "exp": 1768463600,
  "delegation": {"parent":"op:12345","via":"svc-router","trace":"txn-987"}
}
```
ken: that looks reasonable. two tradeoffs: 1) how small should exp be (slo/latency vs ops cost), 2) whether runtime services need to fetch parent metadata for every request (chattiness).
natalie: also think about RBAC: if we add delegation claims, policy evaluation should prefer explicit delegation authorizations and fallback to project key perms. otherwise we break implicit assumptions in dozens of microservices.
sam: for exp TTLs, propose default 10m for task-level tokens, 24h for session-level, and allow overrides via issuance policy. keep rotation cheap by caching verification keys and avoiding parent metadata fetch on hot path.
rachel: agreement on TTL profile. for parent metadata, we can embed minimal parent id + signed proof in token so runtime only needs to call auth-service for non-cached ids (cold path). adds token size but avoids a network hop on every request.
ken: audit-wise we should emit an issuance event to the ledger service with full parent->child mapping (async). that keeps runtime verification cheap but preserves full history. also add a retention TTL aligned with compliance.
natalie: rollout plan? we need a compatibility shim so services that expect old project keys still accept delegated tokens until they migrate policy checks.
sam: propose phased rollout:
  1) issuance endpoint + ledger + policy read APIs (internal)
  2) SDK: token mint + local verification helpers
  3) opt-in service checks (feature flag)
  4) enforced checks + deprecate long-lived operator tokens for call paths covered by delegation
rachel: timeline: 6 weeks for MVP (issuance + ledger + SDK), then 8 weeks for service opt-ins. will prepare RFC and a migration checklist.
auth-bot: New draft RFC created: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/token-delegation-2026 (rachel) :white_check_mark:
ken: small nit — name the claim "delegation_proof" not generic "delegation". helps avoid collisions with future fields.
rachel: good call. I'll update the draft. who wants to volunteer to review the SDK design next week?
ken: I can.
sam: happy to help on the ledger retention policy.
natalie: I'll coordinate a compatibility test plan with platform QA.
rachel: perfect — thanks all. I'll push the draft and link the test checklist in this thread. :thumbsup:
